output: Anthropic launched Claude Code Security, a security-focused product built using its Opus 4.6 model family. The tool can autonomously review large codebases, surface and prioritize high-severity vulnerabilities, double-check its findings, and suggest fixes; it is being released as a limited research preview for Enterprise/Team customers and open-source maintainers, with safeguards and cautious rollout due to dual-use risks.

Figma (Feb 20, 2026) released new Figma Make connectors that let Make pull context from external product ecosystem tools. Featured connectors include Amplitude, Box, Dovetail, Granola, Marvin, and zeroheight. Teams can also add a custom connector to connect any remote MCP server, authenticate, and surface selected resources inside Make. This improves designer–product workflows by bringing analytics, research, docs, and other product context directly into prototypes and prompts, reducing context switching and enabling richer, real-world prototyping and collaboration.

Notion CEO Ivan Zhao discussed a major custom Notion AI agents launch in an interview/podcast; the company said custom agents will launch in the coming week and that a large share of Notion databases are being built by agents — signaling a product shift toward agent-first workflows and potential changes to pricing, access, and integrations for product, marketing, and design teams.

Weaviate launched an open-source 'Agent Skills' repository to equip coding agents (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, etc.) with production-ready skills for Weaviate workflows. The release includes structured skills and cookbooks (cluster management, data lifecycle imports, agentic RAG recipes), six slash commands (/weaviate:ask, :collections, :explore, :fetch, :query, :search), quick-install patterns (npx skills add weaviate/agent-skills), and a free Weaviate Cloud Sandbox for experimentation (14-day small instances, upgradeable). The goal is to reduce agent hallucinations and accelerate production apps; early adopters report lower debugging time for RAG/agentic pipelines.

WordPress announced an AI Assistant integrated into its site editor that allows users to edit and manage websites via natural-language prompts (rewrite content, translate text, adjust design elements like fonts/layouts). For WordPress AI website builder users the assistant is enabled by default; other users must enable 'AI tools' in settings. The assistant can also generate or edit images using Google's Nano Banana models — a workflow improvement for marketers and designers managing site content and visual assets.

Meta has embedded the Manus AI agent into Ads Manager, adding a Manus shortcut in the Ads Manager Tools/navigation (appearing under the "Manage" group) and making Manus available via the Tools menu. The integration provides advertisers built-in agent capabilities for report building, audience research, and campaign analysis (in-workflow prompts and pop-up nudges were reported). Practical impact: marketing teams can request automated reports and audience analysis inside Ads Manager instead of building custom API workflows, potentially saving time but raising accuracy/hallucination and transparency concerns.

India's Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026 (IT Rules 2026) — recognized and regulated "Synthetically Generated Information" (SGI). Key requirements: mandatory visible labelling of AI-generated content and audio disclosures; embedding persistent digital identifiers/metadata for traceability (tampering prohibited); much faster removal timelines (3-hour takedown for government/court-declared unlawful content; 2-hour removal for highly sensitive deepfake intimate material); shorter complaint-resolution timelines; stricter pre-publication duties and technical verification requirements for Significant Social Media Intermediaries (SSMIs, platforms >5M users); failure to comply risks loss of safe-harbour protections. Rules brought into force from 20 Feb 2026.

TechHQ (Feb 20, 2026) summarizes a new NBER working paper ("Firm Data on AI") based on surveys of ~6,000 executives across the US, UK, Germany and Australia. Key findings reported: 69% of firms use some form of AI (41% using text generation/LLMs, 28% ML data processing, 29% visual content); measured productivity gains averaged ~0.29% across the four countries over the past three years (with larger gains in some contexts); executives expect cumulative productivity gains of ~1.4% by 2028; early high-impact case studies (e.g., controlled studies showing ~14% gains in customer support with generative AI) exist but aggregate effects remain modest so far; workforce disruption is limited in early deployments and complementary investments (training, workflow redesign) are critical to capture measurable ROI.

Google rolled out Lyria 3, a generative AI music model, into Gemini allowing users to generate short AI music tracks from the Gemini app — a major model announcement and product expansion for Google's Gemini music capabilities.

Bengaluru-based Sarvam AI announced new indigenous large language models (reported as Sarvam-30B and Sarvam-105B) and an offline AI assistant at the India AI Impact Summit — a locally-developed model launch with commercial and strategic implications for the Indian AI ecosystem.
Samsung announced an expansion of its Galaxy AI multi-agent ecosystem, adding a new AI agent across the Galaxy ecosystem to improve user interactions and device AI features.

Reports of recent startup funding: aibusiness reports a $1 billion funding round for a spatial intelligence startup (advancing 3D/virtual world generation), and DatacenterDynamics reports Emerald AI raised $25 million in a seed extension — examples of sizeable private funding activity in AI startups.

Code Metal closed a $125 million Series B (reported) led by Salesforce Ventures to modernize legacy and defense software with AI-driven tooling, marking a significant funding round in the AI-for-legacy-systems space.

Peak XV (formerly Sequoia India & SEA leadership) announced a $1.3 billion close across new India/Asia-focused funds to invest in startups including AI, fintech and consumer sectors. The raise represents a major deployment of capital targeting AI and regional startup expansion and positions Peak XV as a larger regional investor with significant dry powder.

The Gates Foundation, Novo Nordisk Foundation, and Wellcome announced a joint US$60 million initiative (Evidence for AI in Health — EVAH) to fund locally led evaluations of mature AI health tools in low- and middle-income countries, with the first RFP open and implementation partners J-PAL and APHRC. This is a $60M joint philanthropic investment to generate evidence for AI deployment in health — meets the >= $25M funding threshold and is material for AI in global health.

Multiple technology news outlets (Futurism, Geo.tv and others) reported that at least two AWS service disruptions in December 2025 were linked in reporting to Amazon's internal AI coding assistant (Kiro), claiming the assistant made code/environment changes that contributed to outages (one report describes a 13-hour disruption when an environment was deleted and recreated). These articles were published or aggregated on Feb 21, 2026.

ChipAgents closed an oversubscribed funding event that brings total capital raised to $74M (Series A1 described as $50M led by Matter Venture Partners, total $74M). Strategic investors named include Matter Venture Partners (TSMC-backed), Bessemer Venture Partners, Micron, MediaTek, and Ericsson. Board/advisory updates: Wen Hsieh (Matter VP) joining the board; Sandeep Bharathi joined advisory board. The company positions its agentic AI platform for semiconductor design with reported major enterprise adoption, multi-year licensing deals, and sharp ARR growth cited in the announcement.

The Information reported (widely reshared on social platforms on Feb 22, 2026) that OpenAI is reportedly finalizing first commitments for an unprecedented mega funding round of around $100 billion (reports described it as a potential private round of that scale). This is a high-impact funding report/rumor; it is material if confirmed but remained report/rumor at the time of collection.

Adaption Labs secured a $50 million seed round led by Emergence Capital to build adaptive AI models that learn on the fly — a material funding event for an AI model-focused startup (reported by Fortune).

Google rolled out Gemini 3.1 Pro — an upgraded Gemini core model that improves complex reasoning and creative coding (features cited include animated SVG generation from text, creative coding, and availability via Gemini API, AI Studio, Vertex AI and Gemini Enterprise previews).
Google DeepMind/Google Labs rolled out Project Genie, an experimental web prototype powered by Genie 3 that lets Google AI Ultra subscribers create, explore and remix interactive, navigable worlds.

Samsung announced on Feb 22, 2026 that Galaxy AI is expanding its multi-agent ecosystem and will introduce Perplexity as an additional AI agent on upcoming flagship Galaxy devices. Perplexity will be accessible via a dedicated voice wake phrase ("Hey Plex") and deep integrations across select Samsung apps (Notes, Clock, Gallery, Reminder, Calendar) to enable multi-step workflows; Samsung framed this as a commercial integration/partnership and system-level expansion of Galaxy AI.

Market-moving report that Anthropic released a new AI tool focused on code scanning/security (reported as a Claude-based code/security tool); the story is credited with triggering sell-offs in some cybersecurity stocks — represents a new product/tool announcement with market impact.

Microsoft added xAI's Grok 4.1 Fast to Microsoft Copilot Studio (preview). Practical impact: Copilot Studio now supports an additional fast-reasoning model option suitable for large-context, complex workflows and deeper tool use. Access is limited (preview; US-based makers initially), the feature is off by default and requires org admin enablement, and Grok is hosted outside Microsoft-managed infrastructure under xAI's terms (enterprise data-handling and contractual implications). For product, marketing, and design teams this means easier experimentation with a low-latency model inside Copilot Studio (faster prototyping, agent performance improvements) but also new admin/ procurement steps and data governance considerations.

PoshBuilder AI entered beta with a desktop IDE and a self-hosted CMS option positioned to compete with existing AI coding/IDE tools (Cursor, etc.). Practical impact: product and engineering teams get an offline/desktop environment for building AI-assisted code and CMS-driven sites with more control over hosting; designers and product teams may benefit from faster iteration via a local IDE and integrations for generating UI code and mockups. Availability: beta (invite/early-access); pricing and enterprise terms TBD in the announcement.

HAIL AI™ announced a new class of AI for public websites that embeds on-site AI experiences. Practical impact: enables product teams to add website-embedded generative/assistant capabilities (immediate in-context interactions) without building backend model infra; marketing teams can deploy personalized, interactive experiences and lead-gen bots directly on public pages; designers can prototype interactive content and flows that run client-side or via HAIL's hosting. Access/terms/pricing not clarified in the announcement — teams should evaluate data-handling and integration options before rollout.

Tripo AI announced an enterprise‑grade AI 3D model generator expansion for the U.S. spatial computing market—relevant to design and product teams producing 3D assets for spatial/AR/VR experiences. Practical impact: potential speedup in 3D asset creation and prototyping; check fidelity, export formats, and licensing for production use.

infoCorvus released updates to its ROAD platform, positioning a unified data lifecycle and governance control plane to accelerate enterprise AI enablement. Practical impact: product and data teams get a governed pipeline for ingestion, migration, governance and model integration—relevant for enterprises building compliant AI workflows; announcement focused on platform capabilities rather than specific pricing details.

Clear Ads launched an AI Search Optimization service aimed at making brands visible across AI/'AI Mode' search experiences. Practical impact for marketing teams: new service to optimize brand visibility for AI‑mode queries (potentially affecting discovery and ad strategy); press release distributed via Newsfile/Newswire, no detailed pricing in announcement.

Reports surfaced that Microsoft 365 Copilot mistakenly pulled confidential content for some enterprise users, with Microsoft acknowledging the issue (a material trust/privilege concern for enterprise AI features).

Official publication of the AI Impact Summit (New Delhi) Declaration on the Government of India (Ministry of External Affairs) website. The declaration (dated/published 21 Feb 2026) describes seven 'Chakras' (pillars) and frames outputs (e.g., Trusted AI Commons, Global AI Impact Commons, Charter for Democratic Diffusion of AI) as voluntary, non‑binding measures. The page includes an authoritative list of endorsing countries/international organisations (88 entries) and underscores voluntary, non‑binding cooperation rather than legally binding safety commitments.

Google AI 'Progress Report' / responsibility update (Feb 2026) describing Google's multi-layered approach to responsible AI governance and focusing on agentic/frontier risks — relevant to corporate governance and policy signals from a major lab (pdf on ai.google).

Multiple news articles report Microsoft confirmed a logic bug in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat's "work tab" that, for a window beginning in late January 2026 and lasting several weeks, allowed Copilot to read and summarize emails from users' Sent Items and Drafts (including items labeled confidential/DLP-protected). Microsoft acknowledged the issue and said a fix is rolling out; guidance in coverage urges admins to review Copilot audit logs, check settings, and investigate any exposure during the affected window. Coverage appeared in mainstream tech outlets (e.g., Yahoo Tech, Techworm) on Feb 23, 2026.

Leonardo.Ai announced a refreshed brand identity and launched a Creative Engine API after joining Canva, positioning the product as a developer- and enterprise-ready foundation for integrating generative-creative models and workflows into third-party platforms. Practical impact: enables product and engineering teams to embed generative visual capabilities into apps and pipelines, shifting some creative work from end-user tools into programmatic automation and platform-level integrations.

Wispr Flow launched its Android app for AI-powered dictation (published Feb 23, 2026). The release adds a floating-bubble Android UI, supports dictation across apps, claims a 30% infrastructure speedup versus prior builds, and introduces a new Hinglish transcription model and multi-language translation support.

Picsart launched "Aura", an AI collaborator that generates social content and short-form videos in minutes. Practical impact: marketing and content teams can rapidly produce idea variations, short-form video drafts, and social assets inside Picsart, reducing creative iteration time and manual video editing effort and enabling faster campaign production and testing.

Commotion announced an Enterprise AI Operating System (powered by NVIDIA Nemotron and open models) to unify context, orchestration, and execution so "AI Workers" can autonomously complete business tasks. Practical impact: product and marketing teams gain tooling for automating multi-step workflows (data retrieval, decision logic, execution across apps) which can reduce manual coordination, speed campaign ops, and enable higher-scale automation.

Samsung confirmed Perplexity will be an additional AI agent option within its Galaxy AI features for the upcoming Galaxy S26 series. Users will be able to summon Perplexity (example activation: "Hey Plex") and the agent will operate across device features (Calendar, Clock, Gallery, Notes, Reminders) and select third-party apps. Practical impact: product, marketing, and design professionals using Galaxy devices gain an alternative on-device agent for content assistance, search-style answers, and quick content edits—changing where and how some mobile-first content or research workflows are done.

Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.6 is now available in Amazon Bedrock (publication: Feb 23, 2026). AWS published model availability/Bedrock support notes describing Sonnet 4.6 as a frontier upgrade for coding, agents, and enterprise work — a major model availability event with commercial implications for Bedrock customers and partners.
CNBC reports DeepSeek (a company covered in market news) intends to release a new AI model — a product/model announcement that could affect sector competition and investor sentiment.

ETRI (Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute) unveiled 'Safe LLaVA,' a vision-language model with structural safety enhancements intended to reduce harmful outputs — positioned as a model-level safety announcement rather than a commercial product launch.

OpenAI announced multiyear commercial deals with major consulting firms (reported as 'lands deals with consulting giants') — material enterprise partnerships that expand OpenAI's commercial distribution and integration channels with global consulting firms, with implications for large-scale enterprise deployments.

Amazon announced a roughly $12 billion investment to build AI data centers in Louisiana — a major strategic infrastructure investment that materially expands AWS capacity for AI workloads and has downstream commercial implications for model hosting, Bedrock customers and cloud partners.

Stacks, an AI platform for enterprise accounting/finance teams, raised a $23 million Series A led by Lightspeed (with returning investors including EQT Ventures, General Catalyst, S16VC). The coverage (Tech.eu) describes Stacks' data-layer approach to unify transaction-level financial data, its use of ML/agents to automate finance workflows, its client traction (~30 customers named) and that the round brings total funding to ~$35M.

Humand Technologies announced a $66M funding round (Series A) to scale its AI-powered operating system for frontline/deskless workers and accelerate AI development; round led by Kaszek Ventures and Goodwater Capital with participation from Y Combinator, Newtopia VC and others. The platform embeds AI agents for HR, communications, and operational workflows and is used by >1.6M workers across 1,500+ organizations.

Cadence completed its acquisition of Hexagon AB's Design and Engineering (D&E) business for approximately €2.7 billion (70% cash, 30% Cadence stock). Cadence positions the deal as a major strategic step to expand its System Design & Analysis portfolio and advance its 'Physical AI' and multiphysics capabilities — enabling tighter coupling of physics-based simulation and AI-driven design workflows. The transaction is expected to add ~$160M to Cadence's 2026 revenue and was described as accretive in 2027 (28 cents dilutive in 2026 on a non-GAAP basis). This is a material M&A event that affects AI/engineering simulation and Physical AI market positioning.

Anthropic said Chinese companies used its Claude model to help improve their own models (reporting of model distillation/use cases) — a noteworthy disclosure about model reuse and competitive implications for model IP, export controls, and model hardening efforts.

Anthropic published a technical/security post titled "Detecting and preventing distillation attacks" (Feb 23, 2026) describing identification and mitigation of a class of model-extraction/distillation attacks — a significant high-signal safety/security update from a major AI lab.

Supermetrics published February 2026 product updates introducing Supermetrics AI integrations (official connectors to ChatGPT, Anthropic/Claude, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot) that let AI agents query live marketing metrics via a new MCP Server; a Text-to-Insight (Insights Agent) feature that turns plain-language prompts into structured analyses, dashboards, and data-backed recommendations; a Connector Builder (low-code) for custom web API connectors (early access); Data API availability on all plans; new warehouse destinations (Databricks, Microsoft Fabric) and Data Activation workspace improvements. Practical impact: marketing, product, and design teams can (1) surface live campaign metrics inside AI assistants for faster decisioning, (2) auto-generate dashboards and analyses from natural language prompts, (3) automate data pipelines and BI integrations without heavy engineering, and (4) move from manual reporting to embedded, AI-driven workflows.

Akii launched a developer-first Akii API to expose AI visibility infrastructure: programmatic multi-engine AI visibility scans (Google AI Search, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot), structured time-series citation and competitor data, prioritized action recommendations with impact scoring, webhooks for real-time alerts/automation, and production-ready features (versioned API keys, async job processing, tenancy isolation, RBAC). Availability: the API is live and offered on Akii's Growth and Agency plans; docs/SDKs are published. Practical impact: growth, marketing, and product teams (and agencies/SaaS platforms) can embed AI-search visibility into CRMs, BI dashboards, Slack/Jira workflows, and client portals—automating detection and remediation of brand visibility shifts inside AI-generated answers.

Reuters reports that Anthropic accused three Chinese companies of harvesting content from its Claude model via large-scale distillation/model-extraction techniques; the allegation names firms (e.g., DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax in other reporting) and underscores growing international tensions and security concerns around model extraction and IP/data misuse.

Reuters reported that Canadian officials summoned OpenAI safety team members to Ottawa for urgent talks about the company's safety protocols after it emerged OpenAI had not shared certain internal concerns — a notable regulatory / government engagement on model safety and disclosure obligations.

Reuters reports that Anthropic said its Claude Code tool can be used to modernize legacy COBOL systems by automating exploration and analysis phases, speeding modernization from years to quarters. The announcement was accompanied by a company blog post and triggered market reactions: IBM shares plunged about 13.2%, the steepest daily drop since 2000, as investors weighed the potential impact of Anthropic's tool on incumbents and software firms.

TechNode reports that Kimi's Moonshot AI said it secured over $700 million in new funding and is seeing a revenue surge — a sizable funding round for an AI startup, indicating robust investment activity in the sector.

Questt AI announced Intelligence Warehouse: a product that claims to solve context fragmentation for enterprise AI, delivering up to 98% decision accuracy at significantly lower cost (advertised as ~1/8th the cost). The announcement positions the Intelligence Warehouse as a central store for contextual signals to improve downstream AI outputs and decisioning; practical impact for product, marketing, and design teams includes higher-quality AI-driven recommendations and analytics, easier integration of contextual data into AI workflows, and potential cost savings for enterprise deployments.

SambaNova announced a new chip positioned as the "fastest chip for agentic AI", said it is collaborating with Intel, and disclosed a $350M funding raise — a major AI infrastructure product announcement combined with large funding for the company.
MatX, an AI chip startup, raised about $500 million in a new funding round to scale production and compete with Nvidia — a major funding event in AI hardware.
Basis raised $100 million to expand its AI agent platform for accountants — the funding is intended to accelerate agent-native accounting workflows and broaden the product's market reach.

Federal Reserve Governor Christopher J. Waller delivered a speech titled "Operationalizing AI at the Federal Reserve" (Feb 24, 2026). He described a System-first approach to adopting AI across Reserve Banks, deployment of a common internal general-purpose AI platform for employees, emphasis on guardrails (model validation, human accountability, information-security controls), training/upskilling, and embedding AI into workflows to improve operational efficiency while managing model and operational risk.
Cursor announced a major update to its AI coding agents, adding functionality and improvements intended to better compete with rival AI coding tools and improve developer workflows.

Anthropic unveiled ten new business plug-ins for its Claude models that let companies plug AI into core workflows (investment banking deal review, portfolio analysis, HR new‑hire materials, private equity, engineering and design tasks). Anthropic said the plug-ins connect Claude to commonly used business tools (Google Calendar, Gmail) and were developed with partners including LSEG and FactSet; companies such as Thomson Reuters and RBC Wealth Management are using Claude-powered agents. Companies can also build and manage their own plug-ins. Practical impact: provides product, marketing and design teams enterprise-grade integrations and automation for document review, brand-consistent content generation, scheduling/coordination, and domain-specific analysis — enabling faster, more integrated workflows.
Profound raised $96 million in funding to help brands adapt to AI-driven changes in search/visibility — additional AI funding relevant to marketing/search tech.
Inception (an AI image/agent startup) unveiled Mercury 2, a new model/tech release designed to answer user queries faster and more cheaply — a notable model announcement and performance improvement.

Amazon Ads launched "Creative Agent," an agentic AI creative partner available inside Creative Studio that supports the full creative workflow: product and audience research, concept ideation, multi-scene storyboard/scriptwriting, image/video generation, animation, voiceovers, music, and final ad delivery. It analyzes Amazon shopping signals plus advertiser product pages, brand stores, and website assets to produce creative tailored to customers. Key practical details for product/marketing/design teams: conversational chat interface for iterative edits; multi-format output for Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Display, Amazon DSP, Streaming TV and Brand Stores; localization and regionally appropriate voice options; granular advertiser control and human-in-the-loop editing; built on Amazon Bedrock models (including Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude); and direct integration into Amazon ad delivery pipelines—reducing time, cost, and reliance on external creative agencies. Availability: announced for advertisers in the UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Spain; Amazon states the tool is provided at no additional cost to advertisers (within those markets) and is accessed via Creative Studio. Source provides product details, integrations and the availability/price/access statement.

Notion 3.3: Custom Agents released (Feb 24, 2026). Key points: fully autonomous agents for team workflows (triage, Q&A, scheduled reports, task routing), built-in templates and multi-tool integrations (Slack, Figma, Mail, Calendar, Linear, HubSpot, FigJam). Notion reports early high adoption (thousands of agents built), admin-level controls and logging, and a consumption-based cost model: agents consume Notion credits (free Business trial until 3 May 2026; pay-for-work pricing begins 4 May 2026). Practical impact: product, marketing and design teams can automate recurring workflows, synthesize cross-tool context, and embed agentic automation into content, feedback, and reporting workflows.

Canva announced acquisitions of MangoAI and Cavalry (Feb 24, 2026). Key points: MangoAI brings reinforcement-learning systems to optimise video/ad performance and its founders (including Nirmal Govind) join Canva (Govind named Chief Algorithms Officer; Vinith Misra joins research lab/rl work). Cavalry brings professional-grade procedural motion-design tools; Canva will integrate Cavalry with its Affinity/Canva ecosystem to add motion editing, while stating "everything that is free in Cavalry today will remain free." Practical impact for product, marketing and design teams: native motion-editing inside the Canva/Affinity stack, algorithmic ad optimisation and measurement features from MangoAI, tighter creative-to-performance workflows (creation → test → optimisation), and potential enterprise/paid upgrades through Canva's growth/marketing products. Source reported on Canva Newsroom and multiple press outlets (Dataconomy, Marketech APAC).

Figma release notes (Feb 17–24, 2026) introduced several practical updates for design and cross-team workflows: (1) Feb 24 — Connect FigJam to Notion (pre-configured MCP integration) so teams can generate FigJam diagrams from Notion docs and document meetings/decisions; (2) Feb 23 — AI hosting controls for Governance+ (admins can restrict AI traffic to Figma's AWS environment / Bedrock models) improving enterprise AI governance; (3) Feb 23 — Workspace-level sharing for Enterprise (easier sharing across workspaces); (4) Feb 17 — Claude Code to Figma (capture editable frames from Claude Code prototypes) and model picker in Make (select AI models inside Make); and (5) Feb 23 — Token Naming + AI AutoVariants plugin update (automatically generate design tokens, bind variables, and create component variants) which speeds design-system work. Practical impact: tighter design→prototype→dev handoffs, automated token/variant generation, new integrations (Notion), and stronger governance controls — all relevant to product, marketing, and design workflows.

Adobe Firefly — Quick Cut: AI-driven 'first draft' video editor that automatically assembles footage and B-roll into a structured first cut from natural-language prompts; supports prompt-controlled pacing and aspect ratio, optional B-roll generation/frames, transcription timeline edits. Launched to beta/published coverage Feb 25, 2026. Practical impact: significantly speeds up early-stage video assembly for marketers, product teams, and designers, reducing manual timeline work and accelerating iteration.

Atlassian launches Rovo MCP Gallery: Rovo agents can now connect to third‑party apps via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Launch includes prebuilt MCP skills/agents and partner integrations (examples named: Figma, Canva, Box, Amplitude, Intercom, Gamma, GitHub, New Relic, Replit). Capabilities: pull live data (dashboards/files/designs), take actions (create tasks, update records), and combine context across apps to generate outputs (e.g., draft blog posts, social copy, presentations) inside Atlassian workflows. Practical impact for product/marketing/design: brings live designs and analytics into Jira/Confluence, automates asset creation (Canva Agent creates presentations/graphics from briefs), summarizes Figma comments into Confluence, and reduces manual app switching during launches.

Anthropic — Claude Opus 4.6 release: model announcement (Feb 23, 2026) reporting state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks and an explicit safety profile; includes new cybersecurity-focused capabilities (Claude Code Security) and expanded beta context window. Has system card and safety evaluation claims—relevant to misuse risk, cybersecurity, and regulator/defender attention.
Nvidia unveiled a new AI system called Vera Rubin; CNBC reports it is about 10x more efficient than its predecessor and represents a new system-level announcement for Nvidia's AI infrastructure.

Samsung unveiled the Galaxy S26 series (Feb 26, 2026) with expanded on-device and background AI experiences (Galaxy AI), tighter privacy controls (Privacy Display, PDE, Knox enhancements), and integrations with agents including Gemini and Perplexity to automate multi-step tasks.

Basis, an AI accounting startup building agentic systems for accounting workflows, raised $100M in a Series B at a $1.15B valuation (round led by Accel with participation from GV, Khosla, etc.) — a major funding event relevant to AI in professional services.

MatX, an AI chip startup founded by former Google engineers, raised about $500M in a Series B (led by Jane Street and Situational Awareness LP) to develop the MatX One accelerator targeting pre-training and inference workloads — a large, strategic chip funding round aimed at competing with incumbent GPU vendors.

Wayve announced a Series D that closed $1.2B (with additional commitments bringing total secured capital cited as $1.5B) to accelerate commercial deployment of its end-to-end embodied‑AI autonomy platform; round led by Eclipse, Balderton and SoftBank Vision Fund 2 with participation from Microsoft, NVIDIA, Uber and multiple automakers. Release says robotaxi trials with Uber will begin in 2026 and supervised/autonomy licensing to automakers will expand from 2027.

Axelera AI announced it has raised more than $250M in a round led by Innovation Industries with participation from investors including BlackRock and the European Investment Council Fund; funding will scale manufacturing and commercialisation of its edge-focused AI accelerators (Europa/Titania) and is described as one of the largest European AI semiconductor raises.

SolveAI, a London startup building AI-driven tooling to let non-developers create production-ready enterprise apps, emerged from stealth with $50M total funding (a $45M Series A led by GV plus a $5M pre-seed led by Accel). Company will scale product, integrations and grow engineering teams.

McKinsey (The State of Organizations 2026): Published a comprehensive report (PDF) summarizing survey results from >10,000 executives and nine major organizational shifts, with a substantial focus on AI—noting widespread experimentation with AI agents, low reported bottom-line gains so far, and urgent recommendations to rewire operating models, invest heavily in people and governance, and treat "agentic AI" adoption as an enterprise transformation priority. This report is high-signal for enterprise policy, governance, and regulatory engagement because it synthesizes large-scale leader sentiment and offers prescriptive guidance that could shape corporate approaches to risk, safety, and AI accountability.

IBM Newsroom / X‑Force (published Feb 25, 2026): IBM released the 2026 X‑Force Threat Intelligence Index showing AI‑driven attacks are escalating — attackers use AI to speed reconnaissance and exploitation (44% increase in attacks beginning with public‑facing app exploitation, 49% surge in active ransomware/extortion groups, ~4x increase in large supply‑chain compromises since 2020). The report highlights AI‑specific risks (credential harvesting for chatbots, supply chain pressure) that materially affect enterprise AI adoption and security posture.

Anthropic — Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) Version 3.0: major rewrite of Anthropic's voluntary framework for managing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems, published Feb 24, 2026. This policy update is important for industry self-regulation, deployment gating, and potential input to government/regulator dialogues.

Anthropic announced acquisition of Vercept (reported Feb 25, 2026 across Anthropic and press coverage): Vercept's desktop/computer-use agent technology and team will be folded into Anthropic to advance Claude's ability to operate on users' computers and automate multi-step workflows. This could accelerate enterprise agent deployments and expanded automation capabilities that directly affect business workflows.

Multiple reputable outlets (NBC News, Al Jazeera, Deutsche Welle — all reporting Feb 25, 2026) reported that US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gave Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei an ultimatum to allow the Pentagon unrestricted use of Anthropic models for all lawful military purposes by Friday (reported deadline), or face actions including being labeled a supply-chain risk or compelled under the Defense Production Act. Anthropic publicly said it continued good-faith conversations and disputed some characterizations; reporting cited anonymous senior Pentagon officials and referenced prior classified use of Claude.

Reports surfaced (Feb 26, 2026) that Meta Platforms has struck a multiyear deal to buy large quantities of AI chips from AMD (widely reported as potentially up to ~$60–$100+ billion in multi-year commitments in press/coverage). The arrangement reportedly includes large chip purchases (MI450 GPUs or similar), multi-gigawatt deployments, and financial instruments (warrants/options) tied to AMD equity — a major commercial commitment for AI compute.

CommonAI announced the launch of a Scaling Inference Lab backed by a £50 million commitment; the UK's Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA) has joined CommonAI as its newest member and is providing an initial £16m grant to lead and fund the programme. The lab will test and optimise AI systems in real data-centre environments to reduce inference costs, improve efficiency and accelerate deployment across sectors. This is a strategic, government‑backed investment/partnership to scale inference infrastructure and exceeds the $25M threshold.

Basis raised US$100M in a Series B at a US$1.15B valuation to scale its AI accounting agents platform; round led by Accel and GV with participation from Khosla Ventures and others. Company will expand engineering and ML teams and already works with foundation models including OpenAI.

Wayve, a U.K.-based autonomous driving AI company, raised roughly $1.2 billion in new financing (reported Feb 26, 2026), lifting its valuation and signaling continued investor appetite for large-scale autonomous-driving AI plays.

Confirmed supply-chain compromise of the LiteLLM PyPI package: two malicious releases (litellm v1.82.7 and v1.82.8) were published on 2026-03-24. v1.82.7 contained injected payload in litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py; v1.82.8 included a malicious litellm_init.pth that executes on Python interpreter startup. The malicious code harvests environment variables, SSH keys, cloud credentials, .env and history files, and attempts persistence (SystemD service and Kubernetes artifacts); exfiltration was observed to domains such as models.litellm[.]cloud and checkmarx[.]zone. The compromise is linked to a broader TeamPCP campaign that began with a Trivy compromise. Actions recommended by vendors and advisories: treat any host/CI that installed 1.82.7 or 1.82.8 as potentially compromised; remove the packages and quarantine affected environments; rotate/revoke all reachable credentials and tokens based on blast radius; search for IoCs (filesystem artifacts, outbound traffic to listed domains, Kubernetes suspicious pods/names); rebuild images from known-good sources and pin dependencies (v1.82.6 is the last known clean release until further validated updates). Security research: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 published 'Cracks in the Bedrock: Agent God Mode' (Apr 8, 2026) showing the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore starter toolkit auto-creates overly broad IAM roles. The default roles permit wildcard access to AgentCore memory, ECR, and interpreter invocation, enabling cross-agent memory reads/poisoning, ECR exfiltration of container images (source code), and lateral privilege escalation. Unit 42 disclosed findings to AWS; AWS updated developer documentation to warn the default roles are intended for development/testing and not for production. This is a material configuration risk for enterprises deploying Bedrock AgentCore agents.
